sections.content: Tacoma, Washington has quietly become one of the most attractive cities in the Pacific Northwest for real estate investors. While Seattle grabs most of the headlines, Tacoma offers lower entry prices, strong rental demand, and a growing economy that makes it a prime target for wholesalers, flippers, and long-term landlords alike. Whether you're a seasoned investor or just getting started — check out this Real Estate Investing for Beginners guide if you're new to the game — Tacoma deserves a serious look in 2024.
Tacoma WA Real Estate Market Overview

Tacoma sits at the southern end of Puget Sound, about 35 miles south of Seattle. It's home to roughly 220,000 residents, a thriving port, Joint Base Lewis-McChord (JBLM), and the University of Washington Tacoma campus. These economic anchors create consistent housing demand across multiple buyer and renter segments. The city has seen significant revitalization over the past decade, with downtown renovation projects, new restaurants, and tech spillover from Seattle driving population growth and property values upward.
Average Home Prices in Tacoma WA

As of mid-2024, the median home price in Tacoma sits around $420,000 — significantly lower than Seattle's median of roughly $850,000. That price gap is exactly what attracts investors. You can still find single-family homes in the $280,000–$380,000 range in emerging neighborhoods, and distressed properties sometimes trade well below that when you know where to look. Rental rates, meanwhile, have climbed steadily, with average 3-bedroom homes renting for $1,900–$2,400 per month depending on the neighborhood and condition.
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Deals in Tacoma WA

Not all of Tacoma's neighborhoods carry the same investment potential. Some are already heavily appreciated, while others are in the early stages of growth — exactly where smart investors want to be. Explore the full breakdown of deal activity and property data at our Tacoma WA market page. Here are the neighborhoods worth watching right now.

items: Hilltop: One of Tacoma's most talked-about revitalization stories. Historically undervalued, this neighborhood is seeing rapid gentrification driven by new development and proximity to downtown. Investors who moved in early have seen strong appreciation. Entry-level deals can still be found in the $250,000–$320,000 range.

South Tacoma: A working-class neighborhood with solid rental demand, especially from JBLM military families. Cash flow numbers work better here than in pricier areas, and vacancy rates stay low due to consistent demand.

Lincoln District: An emerging arts and culture corridor with growing foot traffic and business activity. Properties here are still affordable relative to other parts of the city, making it attractive for buy-and-hold investors.

North End: One of Tacoma's more established and desirable residential areas. Homes here hold value well and attract quality long-term tenants, though entry prices are higher and wholesale deals are harder to find.
Eastside: Often overlooked but increasingly investor-friendly. Proximity to Puyallup and access to Highway 512 make this area attractive for renters who work throughout Pierce County.

sections.content: Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Tacoma WA
Wholesale Deals

Tacoma has an active wholesale market, driven by an aging housing stock — many homes were built in the 1940s through 1970s — and a steady pipeline of motivated sellers dealing with probate, divorce, foreclosure, or deferred maintenance. If you're new to wholesaling, read our guide on Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners to understand the basics before jumping in. In Tacoma, a typical wholesale deal might involve contracting a distressed property at $260,000 and assigning it to a cash buyer for $285,000–$295,000, pocketing a $25,000–$35,000 assignment fee.
Fix and Flip Opportunities

Tacoma is a strong fix-and-flip market for experienced investors. The combination of affordable acquisition prices and rising retail values creates healthy margins when you execute correctly. A typical flip in Tacoma might look like this: purchase a distressed 3-bed/1-bath in South Tacoma for $275,000, invest $60,000 in renovations, and sell for $410,000 — netting roughly $45,000–$55,000 after holding costs and closing fees. Always run your numbers carefully before committing. Use our free ARV Calculator to estimate after-repair value quickly and accurately.
Rental Properties and Long-Term Buy-and-Hold

Tacoma's rental market is strong and growing. The city's population of renters is fueled by military personnel at JBLM, college students, and workers priced out of Seattle. Vacancy rates in Tacoma have historically stayed below 5%, and rent growth has averaged 4–6% annually over the past five years. For buy-and-hold investors, neighborhoods like South Tacoma and the Eastside offer the best cash-on-cash returns, often landing between 6–9% depending on your financing structure.

Pro Tip: Military housing allowances (BAH) from JBLM soldiers are non-negotiable income sources. Marketing your rental directly to military families through base housing offices can dramatically reduce vacancy and improve tenant quality.
Tacoma Real Estate Market Trends to Watch in 2024

Several trends are shaping the Tacoma investment landscape heading into the second half of 2024. First, inventory remains tight. Active listings are still well below pre-pandemic levels, which keeps prices elevated and competition stiff for retail buyers. This actually benefits investors willing to source deals off-market. Second, interest rate pressure has pushed some would-be buyers back into renting, strengthening cash flow projections for landlords. Third, new construction in Tacoma has lagged demand, meaning older housing stock continues to appreciate as the city grows.

items: Days on market have ticked up slightly compared to 2022 peaks, giving investors slightly more negotiating room on listed properties.
Foreclosure and pre-foreclosure activity is rising modestly as pandemic-era forbearance programs wind down — creating more motivated seller opportunities.
Short-term rental regulations in Tacoma are less restrictive than Seattle, making Airbnb-style strategies viable in tourist-friendly areas near the waterfront.
Pierce County as a whole is growing faster than King County, pointing to sustained long-term demand for housing in the Tacoma metro area.

How to Find Off-Market Deals in Tacoma WA

The biggest profits in Tacoma real estate come from deals that never hit the MLS. Off-market properties — owned by motivated sellers who want a fast, private sale — allow investors to negotiate better terms and buy at a deeper discount. Learning how to consistently find these opportunities is the most valuable skill you can develop. Our full guide on How to Find Off-Market Real Estate Deals breaks down the exact strategies that work, from direct mail to driving for dollars to building agent relationships. In Tacoma specifically, probate properties and inherited homes are a particularly rich source of motivated sellers — many inherited homes in older neighborhoods like Hilltop and South Tacoma are held by out-of-state heirs who simply want to liquidate quickly.
Tips for Out-of-State Investors Looking at Tacoma WA

Tacoma attracts a growing number of out-of-state investors, particularly from California, where capital goes further in the Pacific Northwest. If you're investing remotely, here's what you need to know to compete effectively. Before you make any offer, make sure you understand how to analyze real estate deals like a pro — the fundamentals that protect you in any market.

items: Build a local team first: A reliable local real estate agent, property manager, and contractor are non-negotiable. Ask for referrals in Tacoma investor Facebook groups or BiggerPockets forums before making your first offer.
Understand Washington State landlord-tenant law: Washington has relatively tenant-friendly laws, including specific notice requirements for eviction and rent increases. Know the rules before you buy.
Use data to find the right neighborhoods: Don't rely on gut instinct from afar. Use market data, crime maps, school ratings, and walkability scores to evaluate neighborhoods objectively.
Visit before you commit: If you're purchasing a property over $200,000, at least one in-person visit is worth the plane ticket. You'll catch things photos and videos miss.
Run conservative underwriting: Remote investors sometimes get optimistic about rent projections. Use current comps from Zillow and Rentometer, and build in 10% vacancy as a baseline.
Use a deal calculator before making offers: Plug your numbers into our free Wholesale Deal Calculator to make sure your offer price leaves enough margin for profit.

sections.content: Pro Tip: Pierce County property tax records are publicly available online. Before making any offer, look up the current assessed value and tax history. This takes five minutes and can reveal a lot about a property's ownership timeline and potential motivated seller situation.

Tacoma is not a get-rich-quick market — no legitimate real estate market is. But for investors who do their homework, build local relationships, and move quickly on good deals, it offers a rare combination of affordability, strong rental demand, and long-term appreciation potential that is increasingly hard to find in the Pacific Northwest. The window of opportunity is open, but it won't stay that way forever as more investors discover this market.
